description: Startup attribution and bounded prediction/physics scratch, 2026-11-11. Sanitized summary; raw traces, sampler profiles, rejected prototype reports, source transforms and production bundles remain ignored in data/scratch/startup-242/.

baseline.identity: Preserved production dist from 241 with exactly these runtime sources. --base report checkout source metadata is not served bundle identity; per-run entry hashes identify the served artifact.

methodology: Pixel 7a / Chrome 156, native viewport, no browser/JIT reset. Final allocation and ordinary campaigns are separate, each before-a / after-a / after-b / before-b; 10 seconds per fixture, two fixtures per run (clear then jam), fresh page/world/Worker per cell, unchanged 180 idle authority ticks, terrain/mesh warmup and idle cadence calibration. Paused manual steps do not exercise active client prediction; initial play costs stay inside measurement. CPU/trace and sampler modes never mix. Sampler-stop GC excluded from natural-GC claims. Prepared roads exclude generation/city streaming; no Deck measurement.

micro.description: Isolated Mac Node 24 restore stress: 37 ordinary car bodies, 200 warmup restores, three ordinary timing trials of 5,000 restores each, then a separate 5,000-restore heap sample (32 KiB sampling, collected objects included). No world steps. Node V8 and Chrome V8 differ; not a physical-phone CPU estimate.

rejectedPrototype.description: Whole numerical-record reuse via Object.assign cut isolated allocation but made restore ~2.3x slower. Manual dynamic-field/direct-field copies remained slower. Final code retains spread copies and only reuses immediate setter arguments and position-history points. Prototype phone reports remain local; excluded from final comparisons.

exactKernelParity.description: Source-substituted independent esbuild Node bundles of baseline/current. Fixed tick/input schedule with delayed delivery and replay backlogs. Authority numerical states/contact graphs and predictor entity/diagnostic records match exactly at all checkpoints; random UUID and tag sets omitted.

validation.build: pass; rebuilt final source before browser/device checks

limits: Allocation samples are estimates of collected and retained JS allocations, not leak measurements or direct GC-time evidence.
Whole-run allocation and cadence effects must be read from final runs; the isolated restore percentage does not apply to the whole game.
The historical untraced startup/late intervals are not retrospectively attributed or claimed fixed.
conclusions: Startup profiling identifies first-use client physics/collision compilation in one early callback, without overlapping GC. Unprofiled historical pauses remain unassigned. The lab clock reset and idle authority warmup are not warm active prediction.
Position-only bounded history and per-scene immediate setter/readback vectors preserve ownership and exact simulation/replay results. Full numerical state reuse was rejected for its CPU regression.
Equal-work isolated Node restore allocation falls about 29%, while ordinary CPU medians are effectively unchanged. This percentage does not apply to total game allocation or physical-phone CPU.
Phone sampled allocation varies across fresh pages. Observed means are lower but no reliable whole-game percentage is established; client replay-step count is not fixed.

Ordinary cadence does not improve overall and startup updates remain. Clear misses one interval per run in both lanes; jam misses 0/2 before and 1/1 after. No claim of zero GC, universal hitch-free driving or a startup fix.
next: Add cumulative client prediction/replay-step and body-read counts to driving reports, then compare remaining presentation/decal churn at equal work.
